answerCheck.reason: A lower-left to upper-right trend means that larger x values generally accompany larger y values, indicating positive correlation.
An upper-left to lower-right trend means that larger x values generally accompany smaller y values, indicating negative correlation.
B gives the intended distinction: statistical correlation permits scatter around a trend, while a function assigns exactly one y to each allowed x.

flags: The reference to a straight line describes linear correlation; statistical association need not be linear.
